newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Two gunmen rob bus in Bosnian Serb territory.
newsitem.headline: Two gunmen rob bus in Bosnian Serb territory.

text.p: Two armed men robbed and harassed Bosnian Moslem passengers in a bus travelling through Serb-controlled territory near Sarajevo on Monday, Bosnian and U.N. police reported.
"This morning a bus travelling from Sarajevo to Gorazde with 54 passengers was held up by two individuals," Alex Ivanko, a spokesman for U.N. police monitors, told Reuters.
Bosnia's interior ministry said in a statement that the gunmen entered the bus when the driver got out to put snow chains on the vehicle in Han-Derventa outside Sarajevo, state radio reported.
The two men demanded that the passengers hand over money and they pistol-whipped some of their victims the radio said.
The bandits hijacked the bus and drove it about 10 km (six miles) down the road before leaving it near Mokro.

Buses travelling from the Bosnian capital Sarajevo to the eastern town of Gorazde must pass through the country's Serb entity. Serbs often stone the buses on the route, screaming abuse at Moslem passengers.

After a 3-1/2-year war between Serb separatists and the mainly Moslem Bosnian government, the country is divided into a Serb republic and a Moslem-Croat federation. Most Bosnians are reluctant to cross into territory controlled by a rival ethnic community.
